title: AI Media and Visual Repository
answer: Keynotes, conference talks, tutorials, podcasts with transcripts, and a diagram and image library.

reading.body:
The repository is a curated index of 18 items across video, podcasts, and diagrams, not a store of original media.

The pattern is curation by type rather than by source or date. Video covers vendor keynotes, conference talks, university lectures, and explainers. Podcasts are tracked by host, focus, and whether transcripts exist. The image library covers architecture diagrams, illustrated walkthroughs, and browser-based model explorers. Each section states what it excludes, which is the useful part: no live episode feeds, no download rankings, no hosted originals.

For AI specifically, the value of a curated list is that the field's primary sources are scattered across vendor stages, academic terms, and individual shows. Keynotes are where model and hardware announcements land, so a video index is one of the few places those announcements are collected in one place. Transcripts matter because they make spoken material searchable and quotable.

What this does not tell the reader is anything about compute, buildings, or power. The data contains no capacity, no siting, no electricity, and no hardware specifications beyond the fact that keynotes are where hardware announcements appear. It also does not say how items are selected, how often they are checked, or whether the 18 entries are comprehensive. Treat it as a starting shelf, not a measure of the field.
